context: Source: CI time-regression incident of 2026-10-25 and an independent adversarial review of the prevention plan. PR #3423 added an autouse module-scoped fixture (tests/conftest.py, _chdb_connections_closed_after_module) that opened a chDB probe session after every module; the fast-tier pytest time went from 327.81 s (run 40143597290) to 1041.10 s (run 40195371347) and PR CI wall time from about 12 to 20+ minutes for about 18 hours before anyone noticed. No CI check measured test time: _project/scripts/fast_lane_ceiling_check.py checks marker composition only, and tests/duration_policy.py's per-test T1 budget is refreshed from nightly data and never sees module-teardown cost spread across tests. Pre-incident fast-job wall time varied 7.8-18.0 min (cv about 19%), so job wall time cannot be a blocking signal; summed per-test junit time is the blocking metric.
description: Catch what the PR gate cannot: dependency install and setup time, runner-image changes, cross-PR creep and xdist imbalance. A scheduled workflow reads the last day of trunk.yml develop runs and their jobs (about 45 API calls; not make ci-usage-report, which is rate-limit-heavy and reported INCOMPLETE), computes per-job p50 (fast, each medium shard, correctness gates) and the fast-junit summed-time p50, compares with the prior 7 days, and opens or updates one pinned issue naming the jobs that rose more than 15%, closing it when healthy. PR time-to-green is not used (dominated by review latency).
